content:
It was a loud, happy morning at Nuevo Laredo's Escuela Primaria 8 de Mayo: students from all six grades — split into yellow and red teams — spent the day running, jumping, aiming and cheering through a 12-activity rally, as the city celebrated Physical Education Month, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The event was organized by the staff of Supervisión No. 6 de Educación Física, who run an outreach program for schools that don't have their own physical-education teacher. Supervisor Josué Rangel Pineda told the paper his team designed the rally with stations of different difficulty levels, so every student could test their physical abilities while practicing teamwork, both individually and in groups.

Parents joined in too, cheering their kids through each challenge. The supervisor said turnout was excellent — happy, emotional families enjoying a morning together.

The rally is part of the October push marking the Día del Educador Físico, when physical-education supervisors roll out activities across schools to keep kids active, encourage them to take up a sport, and build healthy habits for life.
